edges.description: Mural inflammation can obliterate the vascular lumen.
A subset of inflammatory lesions develops fibrinoid vessel-wall necrosis.
Luminal occlusion compromises cerebral perfusion and can cause infarction.
Cerebral infarction can manifest as ischemic stroke.
Wall weakening can permit vessel rupture and intracranial bleeding.

nodes.description: Azathioprine is used as a steroid-sparing maintenance immunosuppressant in CNS vasculitis cohorts after induction therapy, though drug-specific comparative efficacy remains limited.

nodes.description: Inflammatory cells infiltrate CNS vessel walls. Adult biopsy specimens show transmural lymphocytic, granulomatous or necrotizing patterns. Pediatric small-vessel disease is predominantly lymphocytic; its histological criteria remain under validation.

nodes.description: Compromised cerebral blood supply produces ischemic tissue injury and infarction. Focal deficits depend on lesion distribution; this node does not attribute every cognitive symptom or seizure to infarction.

evidence.reference_title: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system: Clinical profiles and outcomes of 45 patients.
evidence.snippet: The initial presentation was ischemic stroke in 15 (33.3%), hemorrhagic stroke in 4 (8.9%), headache in 11 (24.4%), seizures in 8 (17.8%) and cognitive dysfunction in 5 (11.1%) patients.

nodes.description: Glucocorticoids with cyclophosphamide are commonly used for induction, particularly in severe disease. Observational Mayo and German cohorts associate cyclophosphamide-based regimens with fewer relapses. A biopsy-proven small-vessel series associated earlier cyclophosphamide with faster remission, without demonstrating a statistically significant functional benefit. Confounding by treatment selection limits causal comparisons.

evidence.reference_title: Primary angiitis of the central nervous system. Report of 8 new cases, review of the literature, and proposal for diagnostic criteria.
evidence.snippet: Therapy of PACNS with a combination of cytotoxic drugs and high-dose corticosteroids has greatly improved the prognosis for this condition.

evidence.reference_title: An update of the Mayo Clinic cohort of patients with adult primary central nervous system vasculitis: description of 163 patients.
evidence.snippet: Relapses occurred in one-quarter of the patients and were less frequent in patients treated with prednisone and cyclophosphamide compared with those treated with prednisone alone.

evidence.reference_title: Disease Characteristics and Treatments Associated with Outcome in Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System-A Multicenter Cohort Study in 163 Patients.

nodes.description: High-dose glucocorticoids are central to induction therapy, either alone in selected cases or combined with additional immunosuppression for higher-risk disease.

evidence.reference_title: Adult primary central nervous system vasculitis treatment and course: analysis of one hundred sixty-three patients.
evidence.snippet: A favorable response was observed in 85% of patients treated with prednisone alone and in 80% of patients treated with prednisone and cyclophosphamide.

nodes.description: Infliximab has anecdotal rescue-use evidence. A child with biopsy-confirmed progressive PACNS improved after infliximab following deterioration despite glucocorticoids, intravenous immunoglobulin, cyclophosphamide and rituximab. A single sequentially treated case cannot establish efficacy, routine indications or an HLA-defined responsive subtype.

evidence.reference_title: Rapidly progressive glucocorticoid-resistant childhood-primary angiitis of the central nervous system positive for HLA-B51 and A26: a case report.
evidence.snippet: Despite intravenous immunoglobulin, intravenous cyclophosphamide, and rituximab, the patient became comatose, and the brain MRI worsened. Following infliximab, clinical symptoms and brain MRI improved.

evidence.snippet: The destructive transmural vasculitic process with fibrinoid necrosis may cause severe vessel wall weakening, thus predisposing to blood vessel ruptures.

nodes.description: Rituximab is supported only by small observational series and literature review data, so it is best represented as a selected refractory or individualized therapy rather than standard first-line treatment.
